children: Vessels transit the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas in southern Iran on August 10, 2026. Iran attacked US military targets in the Middle East on August 31, 2026 in retaliation for American strikes on an island in the Strait of Hormuz, the first exchange of fire for a month in a war that has engulfed the region.
Oil prices jumped on Monday after the U.S. and Iran exchanged fire for the first time in a month.
Brent crude (BRN00) rose nearly 3% to $90.40 per barrel, as the West Texas Intermediate contract rose to $85.51.
The U.S. said it struck rocket launchers on the Strait of Hormuz, as Iran said it launched missiles at a U.S. base in Jordan.
The rise comes after prices fell by 7% last week, after talks between Iran and Oman on re-opening the contested waterway.
That fighting offset any hopes for a supply increase after Venezuela said the U.S. would help develop 17 oil fields that have 65 billion barrels of proved reserves.
